text:
alex: Quick follow-up from the RFC — folks, thinking about a minimal handshake between control plane and adapters. Can we sketch a "slim" flow before we commit to the full capability manifest?

maria: yes. main goal = tiny probe so Hosted can route without secrets, then optional capability fetch for features.

chris: Agree. Two phases: 1) anonymous probe -> returns model compatibility & latency tier 2) authenticated capability fetch -> returns KV cache support, batching, quantization hints.

sam: Concern: how do we avoid a thundering herd when many control planes hit adapters for auth+capability? We need caching and TTLs.

alex: TTL per-adapter + global lease. Also add a lightweight ETag on capability blob to skip full fetch if unchanged.

maria: For the anonymous probe payload I'm proposing: {"probe_version":1, "models": ["compat_list"], "max_seq": 1024}. Keep it small.

chris: maybe a tiny example response: ```{"compat": ["gptx-small","redwood-lite"], "latency_ms": 12, "tier": "low"}``` No secrets, purely capability hints.

sam: What about auth modes? Hosted -> dedicated/private differences. Hosted shouldn't leak tenant ids to third-party adapters. Probe must not include tenant context.

alex: Exactly. Probe = stateless. Capability fetch = authenticated and done server-side in control plane with proper keyscopes. Also require adapters to support an "identity-less" endpoint.

maria: Telemetry: adapters should return a sample-rate hint so we don't overload metrics ingestion. Also include a short vector of observability labels (region, gpu-type).

chris: Rollout plan: implement probe endpoints in all runtime adapters behind feature flag. Start routing non-sensitive traffic through new router within 2 weeks.

sam: Backwards compatibility: if adapter doesn't implement probe, fallback to handshake v0 which is the heavy manifest. Add log warning and schedule upgrade.

alex: We should spec an HTTP 204 for 'no probe support' to keep client logic simple. 200 with JSON for supported. 401/403 for capability fetch when auth required.

maria: On wire format: use protobuf for capability blobs (compact) but accept JSON for easier debugging. Accept both.

chris: Security note: capability fetch responses may include quantization suggestions — treat as non-secret policy only. No keys or KMS pointers in capability blob. Secrets must be in a separate secret-exchange flow.

sam: Ops: caching TTLs should be configurable per-tenant and per-env (prod shorter maybe). Also tombstone adapters that go stale for >X minutes.

alex: Question: do we version the probe schema? We should. probe_version and capability_version fields. Semver-like string.

maria: +1. capability_version for backward negotiation. If mismatch, adapter can advertise supported versions and control plane can choose.

chris: Implementation detail: prefer conditional GET style using If-None-Match/ETag on capability fetch. Keeps bandwidth low.

deploy-bot: deploy:adapter-probe v0.1 rolled to staging at 2026-03-18T16:04Z :rocket:

sam: Nice. After staging validation we should have a canary on prod for non-sensitive routing. Keep fallback to heavy manifest for any unknown cases.

alex: Action items: 1) eng-runtime to add /probe and /capabilities endpoints (maria) 2) controlplane to implement caching/ETag (chris) 3) ops to add tombstone + TTL config (sam). I'll file tickets.

maria: I'll draft the API schema and push a minimal OpenAPI snippet to the RFC branch later today.

chris: One last thought — adapters should expose a "fallback-mode" string so control plane can pick compatible runtime variant (eg hosted-compat, cpu-emulation). Helps graceful degradation.

sam: 👍 That solves a lot of outages we've seen when a specialized runtime disappears.

alex: Thanks all. If nobody objects I'll merge the slim-handshake plan into the RFC tomorrow and kick off tickets.

maria: No objections from me.

chris: SGTM.

sam: SGTM :+1:
